historical_references.reference: Sanaar was the name of a major city in the ancient Arabian kingdom of Hadramaut. It is believed to have been the capital city during the early Sabaean period, around 1000 BC. The city was famous for its frankincense trade and was an important cultural and religious center for the ancient Sabaeans.
historical_references.context: Ancient city in Hadramaut, important for frankincense trade and Sabaean culture and religion

historical_references.reference: The name Sanaar was also used by the Umayyad Caliphs to refer to a province in modern-day Yemen. During the Umayyad period, around 700 AD, the province was a major center for gold mining and production, which was a significant contributor to the Umayyad economy.
historical_references.context: Province in modern-day Yemen, major center for gold mining and production during the Umayyad period
